title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description:
# Longest Consecutive Sequence

Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive values.

A consecutive sequence is based on value, not on the original array order. For example, the values `1, 2, 3, 4` form a sequence of length `4` even if they appear scattered in the input. Duplicate values do not extend the sequence.

You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [100,4,200,1,3,2]
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** The longest consecutive sequence is `[1, 2, 3, 4]`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [0,3,7,2,5,8,4,6,0,1]
**Output:** 9
**Explanation:** The sequence `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]` has length 9. The duplicate `0` does not increase the length.

## Constraints:

*   `0 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
*   `-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`

examples.description: duplicate zero does not extend the value sequence

tests.description: duplicates do not split or extend the run
all duplicate values form one sequence of length one
two candidate runs compete; 3 through 9 is longest

solutions.name: HashSet Boundary Starts
solutions.description:
## Approach

Insert every distinct value into a `HashSet`. For each value, start counting only when `num - 1` is absent, because that value is the left boundary of a consecutive run. Then count upward until the run ends.

## Key Insight

The boundary check prevents recounting the same run from every element. Each value is either skipped because it has a predecessor, or counted once as part of the run that starts at its left boundary.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Boundary Length HashMap
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain a map from sequence boundary values to the length of that sequence. When a new value arrives, look at the lengths ending at `num - 1` and starting at `num + 1`, merge the two neighboring sequences through `num`, and update only the new left and right boundaries.

## Key Insight

Interior values do not need accurate stored lengths after a merge; future merges only consult boundaries. This gives a one-pass linear solution while showing a different hash-table invariant from the boundary-start scan.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Remove While Expanding
solutions.description:
## Approach

Put every distinct value in a `HashSet`. Repeatedly pick any remaining value, remove it, then expand left and right while removing every visited neighbor from the set. The removed values form one complete consecutive component.

## Key Insight

Removing values as soon as they are counted guarantees that no value can be scanned by another expansion later. The outer loop may choose arbitrary starts, but the total work over all expansions is still linear.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
